cover.alt: Behind every headline are people. The biggest legal story this week wasn’t about AI. It was about who stays, who goes and who saw it coming. Source: Above the Law, 28 October; Artificial Lawyer, 29 October 2026

pageImages.alt: Behind every headline are people. The biggest legal story this week wasn’t about AI. It was about who stays, who goes and who saw it coming. Source: Above the Law, 28 October; Artificial Lawyer, 29 October 2026

Most of them didn’t see it coming. Around 2,000 people at Weil Gotshal. Associates, first years who had only just joined, secretaries, paralegals, BD, IT and innovation teams. Most won’t be in the headlines. If you’re hiring, this is a good week to say so. Source: Above the Law, 28 October; Axios, 29 October 2026

It wasn’t AI. It was people. Artificial Lawyer is clear AI played no part. Top partners left for more profitable firms, merger talks fell through and others followed. A firm is only as strong as the people who choose to stay. Source: Artificial Lawyer, 29 October 2026

Practice management, meet AI. At ClioCon in Boston, Clio showed one platform with AI throughout, agentic workflows and its own AI phone system. The tool you already use is becoming your AI tool. Source: Legal IT Insider, 26 October; LawSites, 29 October 2026

Less prompting, more doing. Anthropic launched ready‑made legal tools in Claude, from cite checks to matter boards, plus 60+ legal connectors. Claude does the first pass. Your lawyers still sign. Source: Anthropic, 28 October 2026

cover.alt: 60% of in‑house teams expect lower fees when firms use AI. 54% say AI has already cut the work they send out. Source: Everlaw & Wakefield Research, 300 US in‑house professionals, Oct 2026

pageImages.alt: 60% of in‑house teams expect lower fees when firms use AI. 54% say AI has already cut the work they send out. Source: Everlaw & Wakefield Research, 300 US in‑house professionals, Oct 2026
Your client thinks AI cut your hours. So when the invoice looks the same as last year, what’s the answer?

72% → 44% of legal work billed by the hour, today vs in two to three years. That’s legal leaders’ own forecast. 78% say cost reduction is what they want from their firms’ use of AI. Source: Deloitte, The AI Imperative, 121 senior legal leaders, Jul 2026

Start with what AI actually changed. When we run workflow sessions in firms as part of our academy, we start with one question: which steps of the matter did AI change? Most teams can’t answer it yet. You can’t offer clients more until you can.
One question for law firm partners When a client asks what AI saved them, what’s your answer? A discount, or a better service they couldn’t buy before?

cover.alt: Legal Technology Evaluation Checklist W H A T T O A S K B E F O R E , D U R I N G A N D A F T E R A D E M O

pageImages.alt: Legal Technology Evaluation Checklist W H A T T O A S K B E F O R E , D U R I N G A N D A F T E R A D E M O

A trial is not a quick test. It’s a real simulation of how your team works, on your most complex contracts and tasks, under an NDA and data agreement, run by the lawyers who will use it every day. How it handles your hardest work tells you more than any demo can.

Does it fit how you work? 0 1 Have you mapped five use cases as they work today, and asked them to set each up? 0 2 Does it work inside Word, Outlook and your DMS, with your permissions? 0 3 Does it handle your jurisdictions, laws and languages? 0 4 Will a real team build your playbook from your positions?

Then ask the governance questions. 0 1 Where will your data be stored, and is that allowed for your clients and regulators? 0 2 Are prompts and outputs kept, and is any of it used for training? 0 3 Which AI model sits underneath, and can that change? 0 4 Can you take your data and playbooks with you if you leave?
One question for in‑house teams Who will own it after launch? Go live is the start, not the finish. Someone has to own the training, the feedback and the playbook as your work changes.

cover.alt: Legal AI now lives in the document you already use. Microsoft has launched Copilot for legal. What it changes for legal teams, and what it doesn’t. Source: Microsoft; Legal IT Insider, 15 October 2026

pageImages.alt: Legal AI now lives in the document you already use. Microsoft has launched Copilot for legal. What it changes for legal teams, and what it doesn’t. Source: Microsoft; Legal IT Insider, 15 October 2026

20+ purpose-built legal skills, in Word and Cowork. Review against playbooks, draft from approved precedents, track obligations and build case chronologies. Source: Microsoft; Legal IT Insider; LawSites, 15 October 2026

Switched on in Word by default. → Enabled in Word for every Microsoft 365 Copilot commercial licence holder, including non‑legal users → Cowork users add the legal plugin themselves → Partner plugins include Harvey, Legora, iManage and Docusign Nobody has to turn it on. Source: Microsoft Learn; LawSites, 15 October 2026

Microsoft’s own counsel on the benefit: “For me, the real benefit of Copilot is that I don’t have to change how I work.” Aneesh Mehta, Senior Corporate Counsel, Microsoft The skills work from your playbooks, precedents and permissions. Source: Legal IT Insider; Artificial Lawyer, 15 October 2026
One question for legal teams Who outside legal will use this first? Set up the routes into legal now, or “Copilot checked it” becomes the sign‑off.
